newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar profit-taking.

text.p: The won closed Thursday's tight range trade higher against the U.S. unit on dollar profit-taking and anticipation of inflowing foreign funds, dealers said.
"Longs took profits as they believe further rises on the dollar will take a time," said a foreign bank dealer.
The won closed at 894.70 from Wednesday's close of 895.00. After opening at 895.80, it fell to 896.20 on advanced dollar buying for importer deals.
"But the underlying market sentiment is bearish toward the dollar on expected foreign fund inflow next month for investment in the Seoul stock market," said a domestic bank dealer.

South Korea will raise the foreign stock holding ceiling to 23 percent effective from May 1 against currently 20 percent. The finance ministry said it forecast about $3 billion would inflow with the expansion but analysts warned the government was too optimistic.
Dealers said strengthening dollar against the yen in world markets briefly boosted the dollar versus the won.
About $300 million importer deals by Korea Gas Corp due on Monday would be a variable to bolster the dollar, they said.
Friday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 895.40 against 896.00 today. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
